title: Stage-splitter: kernel-aware prefill/decode scheduler to reduce tail latency and improve fairness
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement a new prefill/decode scheduling policy (named 'stage-splitter') that splits requests into logical stages to better align kernel selection, KV-cache affinity, and attention-cost estimates. Goal: reduce p95/p99 decode latency by avoiding long tail amplification when expensive kernels and large attention windows coincide, without regressing overall throughput or cache hit efficiency.
acceptance_criteria: p95 decode latency reduced by >= 15% on mixed workload benchmark compared to current hybrid-arbiter baseline
No more than 5% throughput regression on steady-state long-seq workloads at 95th percentile load
Scheduler integrates with kernel selection hint API and exposes per-request routing tags to observability (console-2026.03)
Rollout flag and kill-switch implemented; can be A/B tested per-customer via rollout config
Automated regression tests covering small/medium/long sequence mixes and attention-heavy prompts in CI
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Spike complete; micro-slicing idea validated on local farm. Synthetic mix (30% long-prefill, 70% short) showed 18% p95 improvement when grouping by stage affinity.
2026-03-12: Prototype scheduler injected into runtime. Implemented kernel-aware routing hook and lightweight per-request cost estimator for attention compute.
2026-03-13: Bench results: p95 -18%, p99 -12% on mixed benchmark; observed 6.5% throughput drop on steady long-seq run when stage merging disabled.
2026-03-14: Design review with runtime and infra teams. Agreed to add opportunistic fastpath that bypasses stage split when KV cache is hot to regain throughput.
2026-03-14: QA: identified a memory accounting issue in micro-slice metadata causing spikes under extreme concurrency (ticketed below as follow-up).
decisions: Prefer soft-stage boundaries (heuristic-driven micro-slicing) over strict phase splitting to avoid starvation of short requests.
Integrate kernel selection hints rather than hard-binding kernels; runtime will pick kernels but favors scheduled grouping to maximize locality.
Expose per-request routing tag to observability pipeline for post-deployment analysis (traceable in console-2026.03 dashboards).
tradeoffs: Latency vs throughput: splitting into more stages reduces tail latency but can reduce batching efficiency for long uniform workloads; mitigated by opportunistic merge fastpath.
Complexity vs correctness: scheduler adds additional heuristics (attention-cost estimator) that may need tuning across model families; plan to gate by model family initially.
KV cache affinity vs fairness: prefer grouping to exploit KV reuse but include starvation guards to ensure short low-cost requests are not delayed indefinitely.
next_steps: Fix memory accounting bug in micro-slice metadata and add stress test
Add model-family gating and default heuristic parameters for Llama/OPT families
Implement observability heatmap for kernel-routing vs latency to tune fastpath thresholds
Plan A/B rollout with Canary group (10% traffic) after fixes and extended benchmark
